entries.d: Formerly 500 Startups. Runs accelerators worldwide and invests across emerging markets including India.
Accelerator fund in the Venture Catalysts group, writing first cheques into cohort companies.
Accel’s pre-seed programme for pre-product founders. The Atoms AI Cohort 2026 co-invests up to $2M with Google’s AI Futures Fund; Atoms X, with Prosus, backs frontier tech at $500K–$2M.
Enterprise-only accelerator for startups whose revenue comes from other businesses rather than consumers.
Global day-zero residency operating in 25+ cities including Bengaluru and Delhi. Find a co-founder, build, then raise from Antler.
Cloud credits and technical support for early startups, equity-free. Often the largest single cost saving for a pre-revenue team.
Accelerator and early-stage fund founded by Infosys co-founders Kris Gopalakrishnan and S.D. Shibulal.
Talent-first: joins before a company exists, pairs co-founders, then invests. Reported terms are 8% fully diluted for $125,000 plus an optional $125,000 uncapped MFN SAFE. Runs a Bengaluru cohort.
Three-month equity-free programme for Indian startups, currently AI-first. Requires both CEO and CTO to attend sessions.
Zero-equity accelerator — takes no stake at all, awarding cash prizes at the end of each programme instead.
Self-serve, equity-free: Azure and OpenAI credits, tooling and support with no application committee.
Equity-free programme for AI and data-science startups — hardware discounts, credits and engineering access.
India-focused accelerator working with very early founders, including pre-revenue and idea stage.
Corporate-innovation platform running vertical accelerators and connecting startups to enterprise pilots worldwide.
Hard-tech and life-science programmes (HAX for robotics and industrial, IndieBio for biotech) that fund at the prototype stage.
The most selective seed programme run from India. Raised its ceiling from $3M to $5M with Surge 12 in September 2026; 16-week programme, 180+ startups backed since 2019.
Since the April 2025 terms update: $20,000 for 5% common on a post-money CEA, plus a $200,000 uncapped MFN SAFE. Runs dozens of themed programmes worldwide.

The standard deal is $125,000 for a fixed 7% on a post-money SAFE plus $375,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE — identical for everyone, no negotiation. Note: since January 2026 YC limits eligible investment jurisdictions to the US, Cayman Islands and Singapore, so Indian founders typically need to flip.
Mumbai accelerator with a fintech focus and a long-running women-founders programme.
Indian Angel Network co-founder and Indifi CEO; long-standing figure in the Delhi NCR early-stage scene.
boAt co-founder and Shark Tank India judge; heavily concentrated in consumer brands.
Shaadi.com and People Group founder, Shark Tank India judge. Early in Ola, Druva and Rapido.
TaxiForSure and Koo co-founder; also a partner at the early-stage fund Good Capital.
Flipkart co-founder, now investing personally and through his own vehicles across India and South East Asia.
Freshworks founder, now investing through Together Fund and a central figure in the SaaSBoomi community.
Ex-Google, Facebook, Square and DoorDash. One of the most active angels backing Indian-origin founders globally.
Infosys co-founder, investing through Pratithi Investments with a research and deep-science bias.
Snapdeal co-founder; invests personally and through Titan Capital, reported at 130+ bets.
CRED and FreeCharge founder, consistently ranked India’s most active angel by deal count — reported at 190–250+ investments. Razorpay, Unacademy, Spinny.
Emcure Pharmaceuticals executive director and Shark Tank India judge, investing across health and consumer.
Zerodha co-founder. Invests mainly through Rainmatter, with no fund life and no pressure to exit.
Managing Director at Peak XV and one of India’s most prolific individual angels before that; ex-Google India head.
Livspace co-founder, among the most active Indian operator-angels by deal count.
Snapdeal co-founder and the other half of Titan Capital. Mamaearth, Urban Company, Razorpay, Credgenics.
Founder and partner at 100X.VC, and one of India’s longest-running individual angels — 250+ personal investments.
Paytm founder; an early angel in several Indian consumer and fintech companies.
SUGAR Cosmetics co-founder and Shark Tank India judge; consumer and beauty brands.
Syndicate and rolling-fund infrastructure; the default rails for Indian angels running their own syndicates.
South-India angel group investing in early-stage companies across sectors.
Angel network anchored in the Hyderabad ecosystem alongside T-Hub.
India’s oldest and largest angel network, founded 2006 by Saurabh Srivastava, Alok Mittal and others. Also operates a SEBI-registered fund.
One of India’s most active investors by deal count — reportedly 36 rounds in 2025. Pools 20,000+ members into single rounds.
Angel network with roots in the IIT Bombay alumni ecosystem.
Online angel-investing platform that handles syndication, diligence and the paperwork for startup rounds.
Long-running angel platform syndicating cheques from high-net-worth individuals into early rounds.
Chapter-level angel groups attached to TiE, investing in companies from within the TiE network.
India’s largest integrated incubator and angel network, with the 9Unicorns accelerator fund alongside it.
The hackathon backbone of Indian tech and, in practice, the best place to find a technical co-founder.
One of India’s largest grassroots startup communities, running frequent small meetups across many cities.
Volunteer-run founder community that has been running Startup Saturday meetups across Indian cities for well over a decade.
Bootstrapper community focused on revenue over fundraising — useful counterweight if you are not raising.
Think tank and volunteer community behind India Stack, UPI advocacy and the software product industry’s policy work.
The Indian IT industry body. Beyond lobbying, its startup programmes and reports are a standard reference point.
Cohort-based founder community; useful mainly for the network and co-founder matching rather than capital.
Professional network built for Indian software people — profiles, projects and a job board founders actually use for hiring.
Launch platform and community; still the default first public launch for a consumer or SaaS product.
The largest public Indian startup forum. Noisy, but the only one where failures and rough numbers get discussed openly.
The community behind India’s SaaS wave — annual conference, founder-only forums and a strong Chennai–Bengaluru axis.
Community and fund for people in the “before the idea” phase, with an India presence and a founder fellowship.
Google-backed global founder community with chapters in several Indian cities running regular fireside events.
Large Indian product-management community running events, cohorts and a job board.
Open community running regular virtual networking sessions for Indian founders, with an active Telegram group.
The Indus Entrepreneurs — the largest Indian-origin founder network, with chartered chapters in most Indian cities and worldwide. Runs mentoring, TiEcon events and chapter-level angel groups.
Y Combinator’s free, open course and founder directory — the curriculum without the equity.
Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council’s Ignition Grant — early, equity-free money for biotech and life-science ideas.
Government guarantee that lets lenders extend credit to DPIIT-recognised startups without collateral. The ceiling was doubled to ₹20 crore in May 2025.
Not money, but the gate in front of it: without DPIIT recognition you are ineligible for the Seed Fund Scheme, the Fund of Funds, the credit guarantee and the startup tax benefits.

A ₹10,000 crore corpus that invests in SEBI-registered AIFs, which then invest in startups. Founders cannot apply — you benefit by raising from a supported fund. FFS 2.0, a further ₹10,000 crore, was notified in April 2026.
Rajasthan’s startup platform offering incubation, grants and government procurement access.
Karnataka’s grant programme for early startups, selected through a competitive ELEVATE cohort.
One of India’s most active state startup agencies, with incubation space, grants and a soft-loan programme.
Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs — grant support for ICT and emerging-technology startups through designated incubators.
Department of Science and Technology grant for hardware prototypes — money for founders with an idea and no company yet.

DPIIT’s main non-dilutive scheme, with a ₹945 crore corpus. Up to ₹20 lakh as an equity-free grant for proof of concept, plus up to ₹50 lakh as convertible debt for market entry — paid out through selected incubators, not directly.
A national network of incubators funded by Atal Innovation Mission under NITI Aayog, spread across tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms — life sciences, bio-pharma and medtech, largely grant-funded.
Large campus in north Karnataka focused on entrepreneurship outside the metros.
IIT Delhi’s Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer, commercialising campus research.
Formerly CIIE.CO, the IIM Ahmedabad incubator. Strong in cleantech, fintech and impact, and anchors the Bharat Innovation Fund.
One of India’s most productive deep-tech incubators; Ather Energy and a long line of EV, robotics and climate companies started here.
Technology business incubator in Odisha, strong in biotech and rural technology.
Industry-body programme offering warehouse space, credits and enterprise introductions across several Indian cities.
IIM Bangalore’s incubator, running since 2000. Takes founders from idea and prototype stage, with dedicated women, climate and social-enterprise tracks.
Europe’s long-running first-cheque fund and founder network, often described as Europe’s YC equivalent.
IIT Kanpur’s incubation centre, which also administers the SIDBI–iDEX seed fund for defence startups.
IIT Bombay’s technology business incubator — ideaForge and other hardware companies came through it.
Backs science and technology ventures aimed at social and environmental problems, from lab to market.
Rajasthan incubator run with CIIE, supporting founders outside the main startup hubs.
The largest startup campus in the world, hosting dozens of independent programmes under one roof.
Telangana-backed innovation campus, among the largest in the world. Strongest on corporate and government connections rather than cheques; equity terms are not published.
One of India’s oldest social-enterprise incubators, backing impact ventures in health, agriculture and climate.
Writes a fixed first cheque on an iSAFE note, in cohort-style classes, regardless of sector or founder pedigree. Founded by Sanjay Mehta.
Pre-seed and seed micro-VC named for when founders actually work.
Aviral Bhatnagar’s day-one fund, which closed roughly ₹100 crore — part of the 2025–26 wave of new Indian micro-VCs.
Pre-seed micro-VC that aims to be the first institutional money in, run by Kushal Bhagia.
Day-zero investor: a residency where founders find co-founders and form companies, then raise a pre-seed cheque from Antler itself.
Micro-VC run by Anirudh Damani; announced a first close of about ₹250 crore for its second fund.
Vaibhav Domkundwar’s pre-seed fund, an early backer of Open, Jupiter and Khatabook.
Pre-seed fund backing young, often first-time founders.
As the name says — India’s earliest institutional cheque, deliberately small and fast.
Pre-seed micro-VC writing first cheques into platform businesses.
Sector-agnostic, tech-first pre-seed fund that also runs an accelerator track.
Cross-border US–India fund where a partner typically reads inbound directly.
Small, fast pre-seed fund that frequently co-invests alongside angels.
B2B SaaS fund run by operators, investing in Indian software companies selling abroad.
Founded 2022; raised about ₹200 crore to invest at seed and pre-Series A.
Pre-seed micro-VC with a bias toward technical founders.
Zerodha’s investment and incubation arm. Unusually patient capital — no fund life, no forced exits — across fintech, climate and health.
Consumer-brand micro-VC backing early D2C and food businesses.
Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal’s fund — over 250 seed bets including Ola, Razorpay, Mamaearth and Urban Company. Runs a structured Winter/Summer programme.
Early-stage fund investing across fintech, deep tech and enterprise software.
Deep-tech-only seed fund; the published route in is investor relations rather than a founder form.
US-based fund backing Indian-origin founders building for global markets.
Seed-to-Series-A firm founded by Pranav Pai and Siddarth Pai. Licious, Darwinbox, Jupiter and Open among its portfolio.
Growth-stage firm founded by ex-Sequoia India partners, writing larger cheques into proven businesses.
Backed Flipkart, Swiggy, Freshworks and Urban Company. Runs the Atoms pre-seed programme as its earliest entry point.
Venture debt rather than equity — non-dilutive capital for startups that have already raised institutional equity.
Backs technology for the next half-billion Indians — agritech, health and deep science. CropIn, Captain Fresh.
Invests in “Middle India” — products for the next 500 million consumers and the businesses serving them.
Climate-tech and sustainability fund backing decarbonisation and resource-efficiency startups.
Deep-tech fund anchored at IIMA Ventures, backing IP-led companies out of Indian research institutions.
India’s best-known homegrown seed fund, founded by Karthik Reddy and Sanjay Nath. Deliberately sector-agnostic and first-cheque heavy.
Formerly IDG Ventures India. Early-to-growth across consumer, software, health and deep tech — Lenskart, PolicyBazaar, Myntra.
Early consumer-brand investor across India and South East Asia; early in Veeba, Chai Point and Epigamia.
Formerly SAIF Partners. Seed-to-growth investor behind Paytm, Meesho, Swiggy and Unacademy; 220+ companies backed.
Consumer-brand specialist — boAt, Mamaearth, Yoga Bar, Slurrp Farm. The default name in Indian D2C.
Formed when General Catalyst acquired Venture Highway; invests from seed to growth in India.
Early-stage fund backing founders building for global markets from India.
Bharat-first seed fund — ShareChat, Sugar Cosmetics, LendingKart. Explicitly backs products for non-metro India.
Investment arm associated with Info Edge (Naukri), the earliest backer of Zomato and PolicyBazaar.
Backs Indian technology companies selling to global markets at Series B and beyond.
Singapore-headquartered fund highly active in India across Series A and B.
Seed-stage firm founded by Sasha Mirchandani. Porter, Zetwerk and Wysa among its early bets.
One of India’s oldest early-stage firms, founded 2006 and led by Vani Kola. Technology-led consumer and enterprise.
Early-stage fund investing across India and South East Asia.
India arm of Lightspeed Venture Partners. Enterprise, consumer and fintech across seed to growth — Udaan, ShareChat, OYO.
India’s first dedicated gaming and interactive-media fund, publisher of the widely cited India gaming report.
India–US fund with offices in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Menlo Park. Enterprise and infrastructure heavy — Postman, Delhivery, Druva, Zomato.
Agritech and food-systems fund investing in Indian farming, rural fintech and climate resilience.
Seed investor known for early cheques into Pharmeasy, Country Delight and Battery Smart.

The former Sequoia Capital India & SEA, independent since the 2023 split. Closed its first independent fund at $1.3B in Feb 2026 — about half its previous fund, with a stated AI tilt. Runs Surge for seed.
Applied-AI and deep-tech specialist, one of the few Indian funds underwriting genuine research risk.
Early-stage fund run by operators, known for conviction bets in fintech and B2B software.
Global consumer-internet investor, long active in India (Swiggy, PayU, Meesho). Co-runs Atoms X with Accel.
Growth-stage fund founded by Sanjay Nayar, former KKR India head.
Pre-seed and seed in hard tech — space, robotics, semiconductors and industrial software. Early in Agnikul and Ather Energy.
Seed and Series A across SaaS, fintech and consumer tech — Mamaearth, Jar, Navi, Zypp Electric.
Venture debt firm lending alongside equity rounds across India and the Middle East.
SaaS-only fund started by Freshworks and Zoho operators including Girish Mathrubootham — operator capital for Indian software going global.
Venture debt and late-stage equity for growth companies.
Temasek-backed fund investing across South East Asia and India from seed through growth.
Seed and Series A fund investing across consumer internet, SaaS and applied AI.
Formerly Matrix Partners India, rebranded in 2024 when the global Matrix network split into independent firms. Early and growth across SaaS, fintech and consumer.

types.blurb: Institutional funds writing seed to growth cheques into Indian startups

types.label: Micro VC & pre-seed
types.blurb: Small funds that write the first institutional cheque, often before revenue

types.label: Angel networks
types.blurb: Platforms and syndicates that pool individual investors into one round

types.label: Individual angels
types.blurb: Named operators and founders who invest their own money

types.label: Accelerators
types.blurb: Fixed-term programmes that invest on standard terms and end in a demo day

types.label: Incubators
types.blurb: Longer-term support, lab space and campus programmes — usually little or no equity

types.label: Government schemes
types.blurb: Grants, guarantees and non-dilutive capital from Indian central and state programmes

types.label: Communities
types.blurb: Where founders actually talk to each other — forums, chapters and meetups
